body.p: In response to amendments are made in response to the Office Action dated November 7, 2024, Applicant amends claims 1, 2, and 4-8 and 10. Applicant cancels claim 9 without prejudice or disclaimer and adds claims 11-13. No new matter is added. After entry of this Amendment, claims 1-8 and 10-13 are pending in the Application. Reconsideration of the Application as amended is respectfully requested in view of these remarks.
Summary of Examiner Interview

Applicant thanks the Examiner for the telephone interview conducted on January 22, 2025. The attendees were Examiner Angelina Shady and Applicant's representative, Heather Kleinhardt (Reg. No. 72,784). During the discussion, the current rejections and proposed claimamendments were discussed. No agreements were reached.
Claim Objections
Claim 8 is objected to because of an alleged informality. Specifically, the Office Action alleges that "by autonomous travel control" should be "by the autonomous travel control". Claim

8 depends on claim 1, which introduces "autonomous lane change control". Claim 8 introduces "autonomous travel control", which was not previously recited in claim 1 or claim 8. Thus, an antecedent basis issue would be introduced if Applicant amended claim 8 as suggested. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the objection to claim 8 be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Interpretation under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f)

Recitations in claims 7-10 have been interrupted in accordance with 35 U.S.C. § 112(f). Applicant did not intend for the interruptions and amends claim 7 to remove the determination unit and the assistance unit. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the interpretation of recitations in claims 7-10 be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Claims 5 and 6 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter that Applicant or the

inventor regards as the invention. Applicant amends claim 5 and 6 to address the indefiniteness concerns. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 5 and 6 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claims 1-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to non- statutory subject matter. Applicant amends independent claims 1 and 7 to overcome the § 101 rejection. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-10 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claims 1-8 and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Pat. Pub. No. 2022/0348227 to Foster et al. ("Foster") in view of U.S. Pat. Pub. No. 2021/0107510 to Kato et al. ("Kato").
Applicant amends claim 1 to recite:
A travel assistance method for a vehicle, the method comprising:
determining whether a route-following lane change along a set travel route
can be assisted with autonomous lane change control;
in response to a determination that the route-following lane change can be
assisted with the autonomous lane change control, autonomously controlling the
vehicle to make the route-following lane change in a first direction; and
in response to a determination that the route-following lane change cannot

be assisted with the autonomous lane change control, notifying a driver that the route-following lane change cannot be made with the autonomous lane change control, and prohibiting the autonomous lane change control from assisting a lane change in a second direction opposite to the first direction even in a case where an operation by the driver would otherwise cause the autonomous lane change control
to assist with the lane change in the second direction.

Support for the amendments can be found in at least paragraphs [0026]-[0027] of the application as originally filed (paragraphs [0035]-[0036] in the printed publication) and claims 1 and 9 of the application as originally filed.

Foster merely discloses in paragraph [0503]-[0504] instances where a lane change should not be performed by autonomous control. Nothing in Foster discloses that the lane change is prohibited, much less it being prohibited even in cases where the execution conditions that would enable the lane change in the opposite direction are otherwise satisfied.

Kato discloses in paragraph [0106] that "[w]hen it is determined that the execution conditions for a lane change are satisfied, the lane change controller 142 starts control for causing the host vehicle M to change lanes (step S 130)." Thus, Kato does not remedy the deficiencies of Foster in relation to amended claim 1. Therefore, amended claim 1 is allowable over Foster and Kato.
Claims 2-6, 8, and 10 are allowable over Foster and Kato for at least their dependency on amended claim 1.
Applicant amends claim 7 to recite:
A travel assistance device for a vehicle, comprising:
a memory storing instructions; and
a processor to execute the stored instructions to:
determine whether a route-following lane change along a set travel route
can be assisted with autonomous lane change control;
in response to a determination that the route-following lane change can be
assisted with the autonomous lane change control, autonomously control the
vehicle to make the route-following lane change in a first direction; and
in response to a determination that the route-following lane change cannot

be assisted with the autonomous lane change control, notify a driver that the route- following lane change cannot be made with the autonomous lane change control, and prohibit the autonomous lane change control from assisting a lane change in a second direction opposite to the first direction even in a case of where an operation by the driver would otherwise cause the autonomous lane change control to assist
with the lane change in the second direction.
Foster and Kato, alone or in combination, do not disclose, teach, or suggest such. Therefore, amended claim 7 is allowable over Foster and Kato.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-8 and 10 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claim 9 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Foster and Kato in view of U.S. Pat. Pub. No. 2022/0135039 to Jardine. Claim 9 is canceled. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 9 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be reconsidered and withdrawn.
New Claims
Claims 11-13 are added. Applicant submits that these do not add new matter and are
allowable over the cited references. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests consideration and allowance of claims 11-13.

It is submitted that this Amendment has antecedent basis in the application as originally filed, including the specification, claims and drawings, and that this Amendment does not add any new subject matter to the application. It is submitted that this Amendment places the application in suitable condition for allowance, notice of which is requested.
The Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at the telephone number listed below if the Examiner believes an Examiner's amendment would expedite prosecution of the Application.
